episode.title: Remove sensitive response metadata and tool arguments from informational diagnostics
episode.before: At parent commit 88d743c3abbef69778dc64a3a776a16510fa77fe, a successful WebSocket handshake emitted the connection URL plus the complete response header map at info level. Completed tool calls derived a printable preview from the tool payload and source, then emitted the thread ID, tool name, and payload preview at info level.
episode.after: At commit 4a36f4549dfce7f7d95bd037a52147c81b79916d, successful WebSocket diagnostics retain the connection URL but no longer format response headers. Tool-call diagnostics retain the thread ID and tool name but neither derive nor format a payload preview. Response headers continue to be consumed internally for status and protocol metadata, and tool calls continue through persistence and execution unchanged.
episode.diff: The implementation changes two logging boundaries with 2 insertions and 8 deletions: it removes response.headers() from the successful WebSocket info message, and removes the tool_log_payload import, payload-preview computation, and payload-preview format argument from the tool-call info message. No test files were changed.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned implementation commit is 4a36f4549dfce7f7d95bd037a52147c81b79916d with parent 88d743c3abbef69778dc64a3a776a16510fa77fe; its subject and body state that successful WebSocket headers and tool payload previews are removed while the URL, tool name, and thread ID remain logged.
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller 4a36f4549dfce7f7d95bd037a52147c81b79916d; issue-bundle.json commit_show_stat and provenance.commit

evidence_units.claim: The commit modifies only the WebSocket endpoint and stream-event utility, totaling 2 insertions and 8 deletions.
Before the change, the successful WebSocket branch logged both the URL and response.headers() using debug formatting.

After the change, the successful WebSocket branch logs only the URL; the response remains available immediately afterward and its headers are still read for reasoning, model, and turn-state protocol metadata.

The shared WebSocket connection helper receives merged and authenticated headers from both the normal connection path and the handshake-probe path, so the changed success diagnostic covers both callers.

Before the change, completed tool-call handling computed a payload preview from call.payload and call.direct_source(), then appended that preview to an info-level message containing the tool name and structured thread ID.

After the change, completed tool-call handling logs the structured thread ID and tool name only, then continues to persist the response item, execute the same call, and produce the same follow-up future.

The removed preview helper returned a marker for direct plaintext arguments but otherwise delegated to payload.log_payload(), confirming that the deleted value was derived from actual tool-call payload content.

A parent-to-implementation source comparison verifies that header and payload formatting expressions are absent after the change while the intended low-sensitivity identifiers and downstream operational processing remain present.
No test file was added or modified by the implementation commit, and the available issue bundle records no status-check evidence.

Normal connection construction still returns the connected stream and server-derived metadata, while tool-call handling still passes the original call to the runtime; the change is confined to diagnostic emission rather than request or execution semantics.
evidence_units.source: git show 4a36f4549dfce7f7d95bd037a52147c81b79916d:codex-rs/codex-api/src/endpoint/responses_websocket.rs, lines 407-415 and 538-543; git show 4a36f4549dfce7f7d95bd037a52147c81b79916d:codex-rs/core/src/stream_events_utils.rs, lines 346-357

candidate_atomics.name: omit-response-metadata-from-success-diagnostics
candidate_atomics.title: Omit response metadata from successful connection diagnostics
candidate_atomics.description: Narrow a successful connection message to its intended connection identifier while keeping response metadata available to protocol processing rather than serializing the complete metadata collection into an informational log.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent response metadata, including potentially sensitive header values, from being copied into routine successful-connection diagnostics without changing connection behavior.
semantic_action.pre_state: A successful connection produces a response object whose complete metadata collection is debug-formatted into an info-level diagnostic.
semantic_action.post_state: The success diagnostic contains the connection URL but no response metadata collection, while status and selected protocol metadata remain available for internal processing and return values.
semantic_action.validation: Compare the parent and changed success branches to confirm the metadata formatting expression is removed, then verify that subsequent status and selected-header reads and both connection callers remain intact.

candidate_atomics.name: omit-tool-arguments-from-invocation-diagnostics
candidate_atomics.title: Omit tool arguments from invocation diagnostics
candidate_atomics.description: Stop deriving and appending a printable argument preview to routine tool-invocation logs while preserving the thread correlation field, tool name, response-item persistence, and execution dispatch.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent potentially sensitive tool arguments from being copied into info-level invocation diagnostics without changing tool dispatch or correlation.
semantic_action.pre_state: When a tool call is recognized, the handler derives a printable preview from the call payload and source and appends it to an info-level message.
semantic_action.post_state: The handler emits only the thread correlation field and tool name, does not derive a payload preview, and still persists and executes the original call.
semantic_action.validation: Compare the parent and changed handler branches to confirm removal of the preview import, derivation, and format argument; verify that the structured thread ID, tool name, persistence call, runtime dispatch, and follow-up result remain.

candidate_workflows.name: minimize-sensitive-data-in-routine-diagnostics
candidate_workflows.title: Remove sensitive values from routine diagnostics while preserving operational context
candidate_workflows.description: Audit each information-level diagnostic at a successful transport or invocation boundary, remove broad metadata or argument serialization, retain only identifiers needed to understand the event, and confirm that the underlying protocol and execution paths still consume the original data normally.

workflow_graph.goal: Routine successful-connection and tool-invocation diagnostics no longer expose response metadata or tool arguments, while retaining event identity and unchanged operational behavior.
when_to_use: An info-level success or invocation message serializes a complete metadata collection or request/tool argument payload.
The sensitive value is needed by runtime processing but is not required to identify the diagnostic event.
The diagnostic can remain useful with bounded identifiers such as a connection target, correlation ID, or operation name.
anti_goals: Do not disable successful-connection or tool-invocation diagnostics entirely.
Do not remove metadata or payloads from protocol processing, persistence, or tool execution.
Do not broaden the change to error diagnostics, payload storage, or unrelated telemetry without separate evidence and validation.
Do not optimize diagnostic verbosity or performance beyond eliminating the sensitive formatting operations.
not_applicable_when: The allegedly sensitive value is not emitted by the diagnostic boundary.
The full value is an explicitly required, access-controlled audit record with a documented retention contract.
Removing the value would also remove it from runtime behavior because logging and processing are inseparably coupled and cannot first be separated.
Only issue-title or classification evidence is available and the actual before/after logging expressions cannot be inspected.
inputs: Locations of routine diagnostics that serialize metadata or arguments
Classification of identifiers that must remain for operational usefulness
Call sites and downstream consumers of the original metadata or payload
A source comparison or log-capture oracle capable of detecting forbidden values
workflow_graph.entry_state: Routine info diagnostics expose the successful handshake response metadata and tool argument previews, although those values are not necessary to identify the connection or invoked tool.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Successful connection logs contain the connection URL without response headers, and tool-call logs contain the thread ID and tool name without argument previews; connection metadata handling and tool execution remain intact.

steps.condition: Apply when a successful connection diagnostic formats the response metadata collection.
steps.validation: The changed success message has no response-metadata formatting expression, retains the connection identifier, and is followed by unchanged status and selected-metadata processing.

steps.condition: Apply when a routine invocation diagnostic derives or formats a preview from tool arguments.
steps.validation: The changed invocation branch neither derives nor formats an argument preview, retains the correlation field and tool name, and still persists and dispatches the call.

validation_ladder: Inspect the parent state to identify the exact metadata and payload expressions copied into routine logs.
Inspect the implementation diff to confirm only the sensitive formatting and now-unused import or local value were removed.
Verify the remaining messages retain the intended connection, correlation, and operation identifiers.
Trace downstream code to confirm response metadata is still consumed for protocol behavior and the original tool call is still persisted and executed.
Run focused log-capture tests with sentinel header and tool-argument values when such a harness is available; assert sentinels are absent and retained identifiers are present.
Run the affected transport and core test suites or compile checks to detect behavioral or unused-import regressions.
stop_conditions: Stop if the before-state diagnostic cannot be established from source or captured output.
Stop if removing the formatted value also changes connection negotiation, response metadata interpretation, persistence, or tool execution.
Stop and separate the work if additional diagnostic boundaries have different sensitivity contracts or validation oracles.
Do not claim runtime log-redaction coverage until a log-capture test or equivalent execution oracle has been run.
unresolved_or_deferred: The implementation commit contains no targeted test asserting that sentinel header values or tool arguments are absent from captured logs.
The evidence bundle does not provide CI or status-check results, and no test execution result is attributable to the pinned commit.
The change intentionally retains connection URLs, thread identifiers, and tool names; whether those identifiers require further masking is outside the evidenced scope.

unresolved_questions: Was any CI, compile, or runtime log-capture validation run for the pinned commit? The available bundle omits status checks and the commit changes no tests.

Should connection URLs, thread identifiers, or tool names be classified or masked under a broader diagnostic-data policy? This episode establishes only that the implementation intentionally retained them.
